subject: botany_2
question_text: What is ICTV? How are viruses named?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.28, printed question 26. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK NOTE: the guide prints "Genes: Lentivirus" in its worked example, where the hierarchy level is GENUS. Corrected on the card.

insider_note: The suffixes are the marks: -viridae for a family, -virus for a genus. Write both in capitals or underline them so the examiner cannot miss them.

steps.label: What ICTV is
steps.margin_note: The full expansion and what the committee does. Four lines.
lines: ICTV stands for the INTERNATIONAL COMMITTEE ON
It lays down the rules for the classification
steps.why: Viruses are not living cells, so the ordinary rules of biological nomenclature do not fit them and a separate committee sets their own.
common_mistakes: Expanding ICTV wrongly. It is International Committee on TAXONOMY of Viruses.
Saying ICTV names bacteria too. It names VIRUSES only.
steps.memory_tip: One committee, one job: naming viruses.

steps.label: The three levels
steps.margin_note: Name all three in order. Three lines.
lines: This is shorter than the seven levels used for
steps.why: Three levels rather than seven is enough because viruses are far less diverse in structure than cellular organisms.
common_mistakes: Giving seven levels. Viral classification uses THREE.
Naming order or class. ICTV works with family, genus and species.
steps.memory_tip: Family, genus, species: three levels and no more.

steps.label: The naming rules
steps.margin_note: Both suffixes, spelled out. This is the mark most often lost.
lines: The FAMILY name ends in the suffix -VIRIDAE.
The GENUS name ends in the suffix -VIRUS.
The SPECIES name is a common English expression
Sometimes a virus is named after the DISEASE it
steps.why: Each suffix marks its level unambiguously, so the rank of a name can be read off its ending without knowing anything else about the virus.
common_mistakes: Swapping the suffixes. -viridae is the FAMILY; -virus is the GENUS.
Saying species names are Latin. They are common ENGLISH expressions.
steps.memory_tip: Viridae for the family, virus for the genus.

steps.label: The worked example
steps.margin_note: Set the three levels out on their own lines. This is a full mark on its own.
lines: The virus that causes AIDS in man is classified
steps.why: Working one real name through all three levels shows both suffixes doing their job in the same example.
common_mistakes: Writing 'Genes' for GENUS. The level is genus. The guide misprints this.
Giving the example with no levels labelled. The labels are what earn the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Retroviridae is the family because it ends in viridae.
